But there is no scientific evidence that is bad for humans. To get the same results as the rats, you would need to apply oxybenzo sunscreen to every corner of your body every single day for a minimum of 35 years or a maximum of 100 plus years. You suffer from seasonal allergies that cause frequent under-eye puffiness.

You have prominent herniated fat pads (bulging under the eyes).

You have impaired lymphatic drainage around the eyes and cheeks.

Filler itself is not inherently the problem.

❌ Poor injection technique
❌ Incorrect product selection
❌ Inappropriate patient selection
❌ Poor understanding of periorbital anatomy
❌ Incorrect placement
❌ OVERCORRECTION

snippet: [Women's Health] Berberine Did More For Women's Cholesterol
caption:
[Women's Health] Berberine Did More For Women's Cholesterol

If you're a woman, berberine might do more for your cholesterol than it does for the guy taking it right next to you.

Hong Kong researchers put 100 Chinese women with mildly raised cholesterol (none on birth control or HRT) on 500 mg of berberine twice a day or a placebo for 12 weeks. Then they pulled stored blood from their earlier trial in 84 men on the same dose and duration, and ran the lipids through the same lab.

In the women, apoB (the protein on every particle that can lodge in your artery wall) fell 0.13 g/L more than placebo, from a starting average of 0.9. LDL and total cholesterol fell by a similarly large margin. Even Lp(a), the marker most people are told is set by their genes, came down (most of these women started low).

In the men, apoB and total cholesterol fell by much less, and LDL and Lp(a) showed no clear change. Triglycerides were the one marker where the sexes didn't clearly differ.

The part I find most interesting is testosterone. It dropped a little in the women and rose a little in the men.

The authors have two leads. An earlier study found women end up with 2.8 times as much berberine in their blood. Berberine also switches on AMPK, a key regulator of fat metabolism. In animal work, estrogen flips the same switch (neither was measured here).

Importantly, the men and women came from two separate trials run at different times, and neither was designed to test a sex difference.

In the end, if you're a woman with mildly raised apoB who can't tolerate a statin, berberine has earned a 12-week experiment run with bloodwork on both ends. If you're pregnant or breastfeeding, skip it, and if you're on prescription meds, clear it with your doctor first. And if you're a man, keep expectations small and reasonable and check it on your next panel.
